newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japan public fund bought US Treasuries - traders.
newsitem.headline: Big Japan public fund bought US Treasuries - traders.

text.p: A major Japanese public fund body was detected buying short-term U.S. Treasuries, possibly Treasury bills, in the New York market this week, traders said on Thursday.

They said the buyer could be Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo). Kampo is regarded as one of the world's biggest investors, holding a total of 95.56 trillion yen worth of funds as of the end of October.
"A major Japanese public fund, probably Kampo, may have bought shorter-end Treasuries in large lots this week in New York," a senior banker said.
Officials from Kampo were not immediately available for comment.
Kampo usually declines to give details of its investments, saying that would invite speculation and affect the market.
The yields of Treasury bills have been under downward pressure recently.
The three-month bill fell to 5.02 percent on Wednesday in New York from 5.07 percent on Monday and the six-month bill dipped to 5.18 percent from 5.24. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
